articleTitle: A digital CMOS 2H adaptive comb filter IC
abstract: A CMOS IC with 2*910 bytes of RAM, A/D converter, two D/A converters and video DSP filters is presented. The converters allow analog input and outputs, while the DSP filters are stable and require no alignment. Configured as a 2H comb filter for NTSC applications, this IC adapts the filtering algorithm dynamically based on the local picture content. The technology and design approach also lends itself well to 1H comb filters and PAL comb filters. Other video processing devices such as time base correctors and picture-in-picture would also benefit.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital processing LSIS for IDTV receivers
abstract: A digital IDTV LSI system based on motion-adaptive three dimensional filter techniques has been developed. This system has applied the advanced pattern adaptive two-dimensional algorithm and motion-adaptive algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application specific teletext-a new modular approach
abstract: A new systems approach to teletext decoder design has been developed which takes advantage of the integration capabilities of 1 micron CMOS technology, coupled with powerful ASIC design techniques. A result of this approach has been the implementation of the teletext decoding function within a single chip. This chip, incorporating high performance digital, analog and memory circuitry, was fabricated using Texas Instruments' standard Epic 1A 1-micron CMOS process. Using the same Epic 1A process, an analog interface chip, CF72303, was also developed to provide the teletext data slicing, clock regeneration and sync separation functions. This chip also combines together analog and digital circuitry within a single 5 volt supply solution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Color-still videophone terminal for ISDN
abstract: A color still videophone terminal for ISDN has been developed. This paper describes that the terminal uses an adaptive discrete cosine transform (ADCT) coding method, and features picture quality and external video camera control capabilities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A single ALU speech synthesizer/ROM/microprocessor system
abstract: Describes a single ALU (arithmetic logic unit) speech IC which includes a flexible synthesizer, ROM, RAM, I/O and a 0.5 MIPS microcomputer with a single cycle multiply-all for less than $2.00 in large quantities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: HDMAC coding for compatible bandwidth reduction of high definition television signals
abstract: The principle of the European HDTV coding system is presented in this paper. This system allows the transmission of high definition television signals in a form compatible with the XMAC/packet standard.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A single chip teletext decoder including data slicer
abstract: The device is a complete, 625 line, World System Teletext (WST) decoder on a single chip, requiring only a handful of external passive components, and one or two external memory devices, which can be chosen from a wide range, depending on the desired system storage capability. Capable of working from a composite video signal ranging in voltage from less than one volt, to greater than three volts in amplitude, the device will process the incoming teletext packets according to the register settings, organise the storage of the required packets in the external memory, and when required, display the stored information via the high current RGB outputs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Quadruplexing: An NTSC-compatible encoding technique that assures crosstalk-free transmission of luminance, chrominance, and two new signals
abstract: Quadruplexing is a new NTSC-compatible video encoding technique that allows full separation of luminance and chrominance information under all conditions, as well as the transmission and separation of 3.0 MHz of additional information which may be used by advanced television systems, such as ACTV. Quadruplexing relies on the inability of the eye (and most TV cameras) to perceive detail in motion. The method doesn't send more information in the given 4.2 MHz bandwidth-strictly speaking, that's impossible. Instead, it sends less luminance information (that part of luminance which the eye doesn't see anyway) and sends other information in its place.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Wide aspect screen NTSC compatible EDTV
abstract: This report is related to a wide aspect screen ATV (advanced television) which is fully compatible with the 6 MHz single channel NTSC system and is being developed and tested as the second-generation EDTV system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Navigation and communications systems
abstract: There has been a growing trend toward incorporation of various types of communications function within navigation systems to create systems which provide greater functionability as compared to navigation systems which provide route-guidance functions alone. The authors, believing that navigation systems with greater position determination precision are necessary in these types of systems, have developed a VNS (Vehicle Navigation System). In this paper they discuss this VNS system, as well as applications for various VNS systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A half inch consumer-use digital VCR
abstract: Describes image data compression, error correction, and channel code systems of consumer digital VCRs. Recording and playback testing with a half-inch video tape resulted in good image and sound signals.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The digital video camera LSI system
abstract: The authors have obtained the first digital LSI solution for a consumer video camera system. This paper shows features of two LSIs, which construct the main portion of the system and achieve much advantage in digital processing and adaptability of computer control.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An analog to digital interface for digital video signal processing
abstract: Introduces an A/D video interface circuit which represents an important advance in the integration of functions for digital video signal processing. The IC includes an 8-orbit A to D converter (ADC), and input selector and a high-performance video amplifier with clamp level adjustment and automatic gain control (AGC). A DAC is not necessary for these control functions because they are performed digitally by the ADC outputs via three simple digital comparators in a time-controlled loop.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: PLL frequency synthesizer for TV set in a new BIMOS technology
abstract: PLL control of a TV tuner oscillator requires few high frequency or high voltage analog functions and counters programmed through a bus decoder. A fast BIMOS technology is well suited for such a circuit, leading to high sensitivity, small chip size and low power dissipation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Eurocrypt-a versatile conditional access system for MAC broadcasts
abstract: Direct payment for programmes is considered to be the way forward, especially for services broadcast direct to the home by satellite. Eurocrypt provides the means to achieve this with any of the MAC standards.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: IHS protocols support new features on the home network
abstract: The successful home network must be expandable, and also 'future-proof': i.e. capable of supporting all features in the units connected to it-even those not yet invented! The European IHS (Integrated Home System) network has a flexible architecture which allows the consumer to keep expanding his system, and supports menu-passing to achieve the 'future-proof' requirement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Common Application Language for home electronic systems
abstract: Home electronic system products and functions from different manufacturers can communicate with each other to exchange control and other information using a flexible and efficient set of services and protocols. An initial set of services and protocols for the exchange of information by application processes in home electronic system products and functions, called the Common Application Language (CAL), has been defined. The language is hierarchical and structured, uses short message formats for simple applications, yet allows long messages to be exchanged by more sophisticated application processes without burden on the simpler.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design process for making CD-I discs
abstract: Compact Disc Interactive is a new publishing medium using the compact disc to bring multimedia and interactivity to the consumer market. Interactive applications on CD-I range from art and music programs to adventure and learning games, from reference aids to tourists' guides and catalogues. The process of creating a CD-I disc is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of rewritable CD recorder
abstract: The authors have developed a rewritable CD recorder for a magneto-optical disk. This paper describes the techniques used to attain high density recording equivalent to a CD's.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An audio coprocessor system
abstract: Describes an IBM-PC compatible audio coprocessor system for the playback of digitized audio samples and real-time digital synthesis of sound effects. Applications include music synthesizers video disc sound-over-still, and interactive simulation systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high performance receiver with graphic displays and a synchronous detector
abstract: A recently developed SW receiver can not only receive conventional broadcasting clearly, but also demodulate and print out facsimile signals. Moreover, the LCD display provides receiving conditions and status. Three technologies, i.e. a high precision PLL synthesizer (10 Hz resolution), a new demodulating circuit and a 8-bit microcomputer control with large memory size support the above mentioned functions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An emulation system for CDI discs
abstract: Describes a system that allows one to emulate a CDI (compact disc interactive) disc in a Unix environment without having to create a physical linear image of its content.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An audio graphic equalizer IC with monolithic filter technique
abstract: An audio graphic equalizer IC has been developed using a monolithic filter technique. This technique has made it possible to realize a perfectly on-chip graphic equalizer without external components, and offers a DC control structure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A 900/2:1/100 HZ upconverter for 1250/2:1/50 Hz and 625/2:1/50 Hz input signals
abstract: A motion adaptive field rate converter is described which converts interlaced 625 or 1250 line, 50 Hz signals for display as interlaced 900 line, 100 Hz signals. Adaptive vertical filtering allows maximum resolution, while minimising aliasing effects.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: FEM calculations on TV cabinets
abstract: Within Philips, FEM is used as a CAE technique to support the mechanical development of TV sets. As an example, the analysis of a TV set during the drop test is presented. The calculation results are verified by practical measurements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Data equalization for D2-MAC signals in cable networks
abstract: This paper evaluates the degradations introduced to the digital component of D2-MAC signals by distortions due to short echoes in cable networks. The use of a Viterbi decoder or a standard equalization technique is suggested to gain an improvement of performance with respect to a single threshold decoder.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A two-chip system for NICAM 728 multichannel sound in TV sets
abstract: Although the recent adoption of the NICAM 728 multichannel digital sound system as a European standard allows a new dimension to be added to TV sets, realization of the most cost-effective circuitry requires a high degree of integration. This presentation describes a system in which all the NICAM receiver functions are partitioned into two dedicated ICs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 100 Hz test-receiver with sinusoidal line-deflection
abstract: Direct view CRT display systems of today's TV receivers with 16 kHz line frequency are based on magnetic deflection and on the unidirectional scanning principle with fast fly-back using an S-corrected sawtooth current. Future IDTV, EDTV and HDTV colour TV-receivers are characterized by higher line frequencies (up to 62 kHz) and a wide aspect ratio (16:9). Direct view CRT's will feature an almost flat screen and a large deflection angle. Due to the short fly-back time, sawtooth line deflection results in high energy losses, higher radiation problems and higher costs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new video decoding and processing system for IDTV and EDTV
abstract: The availability of high quality TV signal sources and the widespread use of large screen picture tubes has created a necessity for improved definition TV (IDTV) and extended definition TV (EDTV) receivers. This presentation introduces a basic video decoding and processing system which provides setmakers with a starting point from which they can develop their TV set ranges to satisfy the diverse needs of viewers and market segments.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Low cost spread spectrum systems
abstract: Presents a broad look at spread spectrum communications systems and in particular discusses the tradeoffs and characteristics of low cost implementations of this modulation technique.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modular video electronic assemblies for solid state image sensors
abstract: Today's solid state imaging sensors require complex timing circuitry to drive them and equally complex circuitry to optimize the output signal. To complicate matters, not only does each sensor technology require different handling, but each sensor is unique. This puts the company who wishes to manufacture a camera at a disadvantage since each camera design which they enter into requires a major expenditure in development time which varies depending upon the intensity of the design. The module concept was created to provide imaging users with a method of achieving good imaging performance without the design time or expense. This paper discusses the design philosophy and performance of a monochrome module and the new color imaging module released in April 1989 by Philips.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Vibration gyros and their applications
abstract: The authors have developed a highly accurate and highly stable low-cost vibration gyro. It is constructed from piezoelectric elements and an H-shaped vibration element. A wide sphere of applications for this vibration gyro are possible.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A multipurpose cordless phone for use in both private and public systems
abstract: The high cost of cellular phone purchase and service still prices them out of reach of many consumers. However, the marriage of cordless phone technology to radio pagers offers the promise of a low cost device with much of the functional capability of cellular phones at a fraction of the cost.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high performance CMOS digital signal processing LSI for next generation compact disc players
abstract: Describes a new high performance LSI for compact disc players which has been developed using a 1.4 mu m CMOS process. This LSI deals with all digital processing except the servo control for laser pick-up and the D/A conversion.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Home THX sound system
abstract: Rapidly increasing use of home video, especially in the Dolby Stereo format, makes this outlet of increasing technical importance to producers. Techniques have been developed to better translate program material mixed for theatrical conditions into the home. The author looks at Hi-Fi reproduction aspects of this problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design philosophy for the RF section of consumer AM radios
abstract: The first basic requirement for the RF section of an AM radio for world-wide use is adequate sensitivity over a wide frequency range. It should also be easy to tune accurately, have a wide dynamic input signal range, be insensitive to interference and have low intermodulation distortion. Building such an RF section with conventional architecture and traditional circuitry requires a lot of electronic and electro-mechanical components. This, of course, leads to reduced reliability due to component ageing, distortion caused by the influence of variable-capacitance tuning diodes and increased cost. This presentation evaluates these problems and describes how they can be solved with particular emphasis on portable short-wave radios.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A compatible road towards HDTV
abstract: Various compatible improvements of picture quality are possible in TV-systems. These concepts can be introduced in DBS-MAC-channels and in terrestrial PAL-channels. A scenario is discussed, in which such concepts are preparing an HDTV-system step by step.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Technical opportunities for the development of world band broadcast reception
abstract: Changes in the design of world band receivers that can enhance the effectiveness of shortwave broadcasting as a consumer medium are outlined. Most of these make use of technology currently being applied either in world band or other areas of electronic design. A smaller number are expected to make use of technology that is currently being researched. Certain of the changes to receivers and antennas are independent of changes in current broadcast technology. Others involve feasible additions to the data broadcast by radio stations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new generation of ICs for high-performance vision IF and sound IF processing
abstract: This presentation introduces a new low-power chip-set for vision IF and sound IF signal processing in stereo TV sets. The improved performance of the IF signal stages is demonstrated by comparing it with that of existing ICs, and by giving measurement results for MAC and digital sound (NICAM) reception. This new chip-set works perfectly from a 5 V supply and dissipates only 0.5 W although it incorporates additional functions and achieves a very high level of performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: FMX Stereo applications
abstract: The specific application for FMX Stereo receivers influences product design objectives, IC selection, and circuit implementation. The practical benefits of the FMX system for home and mobile receivers are presented and contrasted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Auto scan deflection system LSI for multi-sync display and TV receiver
abstract: This IC is designed for multi-sync display TV and is provided with automatic horizontal/vertical frequency conforming which enables it to match the frequency variation of the input signal of three types, that is, separate sync signal, composite sync signal and composite video signal and positive/negative sync signal discrimination, horizontal position adjustment, horizontal/vertical sync processing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ATV and cable-a happy marriage
abstract: The standards-making process is underway for terrestrial ATV broadcasting. 54% of TV households are connected to cable. Whatever standard arises for broadcasting will have a major impact on delivery by cable. A description of the spectrum-compatible high-definition television (SC-HDTV) advanced television (ATV) system is followed by a discussion of the system's application to consumer signal delivery by cable television. Satellite, terrestrial broadcasting and VCR delivery are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital image processing color image scanner
abstract: Introduces a high performance color image scanner which has a variety of digital image processing capabilities such as smooth image reduction and color processing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Communication algorithm for home automation local bus
abstract: Describes a convenient protocol and a bus access method realizing a constant turn-around-time for a pairline bus under the home automation bus. These are implemented on a cheap microprocessor with simple circuits.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Ghost cancelling system for NTSC TV receiver
abstract: With high-quality picture TV currently attracting more attention, EDTV (extended definition television) broadcasting is beginning in Japan. EDTV is intended to improve picture quality, both at broadcasting stations and TV receivers. One of the major features EDTV broadcasting provides is the inserting GCR (ghost canceller reference) signal into the vertical blanking line period. The use of the inserted GCR signal by the television receiver permits easy equalization of waveforms and elimination of ghosts. The authors have successfully developed a fully digitized ghost canceller that is compatible with the GCR signal. They have succeeded in developing a new dividing method as a ghost elimination algorithm. This paper introduces these new developments.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high performance power line spread-spectrum modem LSI for home bus system
abstract: Among some home bus transmission media, power distribution lines have been investigated as a simple and low-cost data transmission medium, since they provide reasonably universal channels to all residences. The authors have already developed a power line spread-spectrum (SS) modem LSI chip, also introduced a total home bus system based on the main bus and SS power line bus. A home control system based on a Japanese standard SS power line bus is now available in Japan. This paper introduces a high-performance power line SS modem LSI that uses a newly developed SS modulation and SS demodulation technique (CSK: code shift keying). The performance evaluation results indicate that synchronization time is greatly reduced and highly reliable transmission is realized.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Processing LSIs for Digital Audio Tape recorder
abstract: Describes the newly developed processing LSIs for a Digital Audio Tape (DAT) recorder. The LSIs consist of a servo processor and signal processor, having features such as high integration and low cost, especially suitability for portable DAT.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Synthetic speech for real time direction-giving
abstract: The Back Seat Driver is a research prototype of a system to use speech synthesis as a navigational aid for an automobile equipped with localization equipment. We are evaluating the user interface by field trials. As this is work in progress, this paper will primarily give an overview of the system and describe its components. Included will be discussion of the map data.base, route finding algorithm, repair strategies, and the discourse generator.

articleTitle: New digital processing technique for extended definition TV
abstract: In Japan, the new EDTV broadcasting service (called 'Clear-Vision') will start this fall. Current television receivers have various drawbacks: interface called 'cross luminance' and 'cross color' due to imperfect Y/C separation, 'line crawling' interference, 'line flicker' due to 2:1 interlaced scanning method, and deterioration of vertical resolution. In order to reduce interference, digital TV receivers such as EDTV receivers perform motion adaptive Y/C separation and motion adaptive scanning interpolation. The key factors to improve picture quality are the precision in the motion detector and detection of the nonstandard signals. If motion and the nonstandard signals are not detected correctly, it is difficult to improve picture quality. This paper describes the motion detector and nonstandard signal detector that play the most important role in this new television receiver set for EDTV.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: IEEE 1989 International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Digest of Technical Papers. ICCE (Cat. No.89CH2724-3)
abstract: Presents the title page of the proceedings record.
